text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters does not verify these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ankara steps up its campaign against the start of Cyprus's entry talks with the European Union, and threatens to absorb the Turkish-occupied areas with Turkey.

- Cabinet is due to decide a course of action on Monday regarding the Supreme Court decision annulling the dismissal of six board members at the state-run Cyprus Electricity Authority. The board members were suspended late last year amid allegations of irregularities in endorsing tenders for equipment at a new power plant.
- Licences are granted for a bank from Luxembourg and from the United States to operate from Cyprus.
- The government slams Turkish EU threats as arrogant.

- Representatives of the United States, Russia and the Western European Union, on separate missions on the island, will have meetings today with Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides on the results of last week's talks with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.

- Nicosia raps Turkish threats on integration of the occupied areas if Cyprus's membership talks with Europe go ahead. Government spokesman Manolis Christofides said Turkey reacted the way it did because Brussels cut short Ankara's ambitions to become a full member.
- Banks enact a half percentage point reduction in interest rates today, implementing a decision taken in March by the central bank.
- Moveable assets in hospitals worth millions are not registered anywhere, resulting in the state not knowing what it has.

- Communist Akel defames the national guard and police with its allegations on so-called illegal actions of the authorities in accepting the voluntary offer of reservist officers in combating crime close to the ceasefire line.
